# Preparation audit: 1L63

*ANALYSIS OF THE INTERACTION BETWEEN CHARGED SIDE CHAINS AND THE ALPHA-HELIX DIPOLE USING DESIGNED THERMOSTABLE MUTANTS OF PHAGE T4 LYSOZYME*

x-ray diffraction, 1.75 Å. Chains of the enzyme: A.

## Catalytic residues

From M-CSA entry 921 (lysozyme (glycosyl hydrolase 24 family), reference P00720), chosen by same UniProt accession; 98% identical to chain A. Positions are carried onto each chain by global alignment.

| residue | reference | role | conserved |
|---|---|---|---|
| Asp20 | Asp20 of P00720 | covalent catalysis | yes |
| Glu11 | Glu11 of P00720 | proton shuttle (general acid/base) | yes |

## Which chain to start from

| chain | blocking defects | findings within 10 Å of the active site | catalytic residues intact |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2 | 0 | yes |

**Every chain has at least one blocking defect.**

## Blocks a faithful setup (2)

| chain | where | Å to active site | finding | from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 97 | 10.7 | Cys97->Ala at residue 97, which the depositors call 'conflict'. Whatever the label, this chain is not the natural sequence: simulating it as the wild type describes a different protein | `struct_ref_seq_dif` |
| A | 54 | 16.3 | Cys54->Thr at residue 54, which the depositors call 'conflict'. Whatever the label, this chain is not the natural sequence: simulating it as the wild type describes a different protein | `struct_ref_seq_dif` |

## Worth knowing (1)

| chain | where | Å to active site | finding | from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 163-164 | 13.6 | 2 residues at the C terminus not modelled | `pdbx_unobs_or_zero_occ_residues` |

## Protonation at the active site

19 titratable residue(s) within 10 Å of a catalytic atom in chain A: Glu11, Asp20, Asp10, Lys19, Tyr24, Arg145, Glu22, Arg8, Tyr18, Tyr25, Arg14, His31, Arg148, Glu5, Lys35, Tyr161, Asp70, Lys16, Arg137. Pass --ph with the assay pH to judge which of their charge states are uncertain there.

## Not checked

- structure-based pKa values: PROPKA is not run, so the protonation section judges each active-site residue only by how far folded proteins typically move its group's pKa
- ligand and cofactor parameters (caterva md strips ligands; see MD_ROADMAP M4)

## Sources

- Protein Data Bank: Berman et al. (2000) Nucleic Acids Res. 28:235, doi:10.1093/nar/28.1.235
- Mechanism and Catalytic Site Atlas (M-CSA): Ribeiro et al. (2018) Nucleic Acids Res. 46:D618, doi:10.1093/nar/gkx1012
- global sequence alignment: Needleman & Wunsch (1970) J. Mol. Biol. 48:443, doi:10.1016/0022-2836(70)90057-4
- BLOSUM62 substitution matrix: Henikoff & Henikoff (1992) Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 89:10915, doi:10.1073/pnas.89.22.10915

Distances are to the nearest atom of a catalytic residue in the same chain; 10 Å is a chosen cutoff, not a physical boundary. Unmodelled stretches are placed by their observed flanking residues.
